tutorial.welcome.title: Welcome, Commander!
tutorial.welcome1: I am PUSULA, your helper robot. Together we keep the base running for 30 sols.
tutorial.welcome2: Drag the habitat and the solar panels from the store on the right onto a good spot. Tap the ground to walk, tap a station to use it.
tutorial.s1.clean: The landing left dust on the solar panels. Tap the solar panels and clean them: clean panels make more power.
tutorial.s1.end: Well done! Every job uses daylight hours, so now end the day.
tutorial.s2.moxie: The oxygen machine is ready. Tap it and make oxygen: air goes up, power goes down.
tutorial.s2.end: Keep enough power for the night heating, then end the day at the habitat.
tutorial.s3.clean: Dust is back on the panels. Clean them to keep the power up.
tutorial.s3.end: You know the basics now: end the day. Tomorrow the shelter opens in the store.
tutorial.s1.build: First the air! Drag the oxygen machine from the store onto the ground.
tutorial.s2.build: Now food: drag the greenhouse onto the ground. It takes 3 sols to build.
tutorial.s3.curiosity: Walk to the Curiosity spot and read the rover's real measurement to earn science.
tutorial.chain.shelter: Particle storms from the Sun can reach Mars. Build the shelter from the store before one comes.
tutorial.chain.antenna: The shelter is ready. Now build the antenna so we can talk to Earth and hear storm warnings earlier.

tip.sol: A day on Mars is called a sol. It lasts about 24 hours and 39 minutes.
tip.moxie: MOXIE is a real machine: on the Perseverance rover it made oxygen from Mars air for the first time in 2021.
tip.dust: Dust is a real problem: the InSight lander stopped working in 2022 when dust covered its solar panels.
tip.delay: A radio message between Mars and Earth takes from about 3 to 22 minutes, depending on where the planets are.
tip.field: Mars has very thin air and no magnetic shield around the whole planet, so particles from the Sun can reach the ground.
tip.rad: The Curiosity rover has measured radiation on Mars with its RAD instrument since 2012.
tip.quietSun: When the Sun is quiet, more cosmic rays arrive: Curiosity measured about 9 µGy per hour in 2019 and about 5 in May 2024.
tip.lettuce: NASA study OSD-268 is about lettuce grown on the International Space Station.
source.rad: Source: NASA OSDR RadLab, Curiosity RAD
source.game: Game event (made up, not real data)
info.power.title: Power
info.power.uses: Night heating, the oxygen machine, the greenhouse and messages to Earth use it.
info.power.how: The solar panels make power while the Sun shines. Clean panels make more.
info.power.fact: Dust really settles on solar panels on Mars: the InSight lander ran out of power in 2022 because of it.
info.air.title: Air
info.air.what: Oxygen for the crew to breathe.
info.air.uses: Breathing uses it every sol. A cold night without heating uses even more.
info.air.how: Make oxygen at the oxygen machine. It needs power.
info.air.fact: Mars air is mostly carbon dioxide. The real MOXIE machine on the Perseverance rover turned it into oxygen.
info.food.title: Food
info.food.uses: The crew eats one portion every night.
info.food.how: Tend the plants in the greenhouse. Do not leave them alone for too long.
info.food.fact: NASA study OSD-268 is about lettuce grown on the International Space Station.
info.dose.title: Storm dose
info.dose.what: The share of the mission's storm dose budget that is used. Only particle storms count: everyday cosmic rays are not counted. This is a game scale.
info.dose.uses: Particle storms from the Sun fill it. The real curve measured by Curiosity decides how fast.
info.dose.how: Make the shelter stronger before a storm and wait inside while it lasts. The gauge never goes down.
info.dose.fact: Curiosity's RAD instrument measures radiation on Mars. In this month its quiet level was {rate} µGy per hour. In the game 1 point is {uGy} µGy of storm dose.
info.science.title: Science
info.science.what: Stars for what the crew learns on Mars.
info.science.uses: Nothing uses it up. More science gives a better mission result.
info.science.how: Read Curiosity's measurement and scan a rock, once per sol each.
info.science.fact: The Curiosity rover has explored Gale Crater on Mars since 2012.
event.dust.fact: Dust storms are real on Mars: in 2018 one covered the whole planet. This storm is made up for the game.

event.reply.fact: A radio message between Mars and Earth takes from about 3 to 22 minutes, depending on where the planets are.

result.key.cold: On sol {n} the power ran out at night. The heating stopped and the cold used up extra air.

learned.title: What we learned
learned.air: Air is used every night. Making oxygen needs power, so power and air must be planned together.
learned.food: Plants need regular care. A greenhouse left alone gives less food.
learned.shelter: Particle storms from the Sun come and go. A thick layer of soil stops most of them, so astronauts wait in a shelter.
learned.delay: A radio message needs many minutes to cross space. Astronauts on Mars cannot wait for Earth: they decide themselves.
learned.rescue: Talking to Earth takes planning: first build the antenna, then send a message, then wait for the answer.
learned.power: Solar panels only work in sunlight, and dust makes them weaker. Power must be saved for the cold night.

concept.sol.title: A Mars day
concept.sol.capsule: A sol is one day on Mars. It lasts about 24 hours and 39 minutes, a little longer than a day on Earth.
concept.sol.question: A day on Mars is called a ___.
concept.sol.explain: Sol is the name for one Mars day: about 24 hours 39 minutes.
concept.moxie.title: MOXIE
concept.moxie.capsule: MOXIE was a small machine on the Perseverance rover. From 2021 to 2023 it really made oxygen from the carbon dioxide in Mars air.
concept.moxie.question: On Mars, MOXIE made ___ from the air.
concept.moxie.explain: MOXIE split carbon dioxide and made 122 grams of oxygen in all: about what a small dog breathes in 10 hours.
concept.regolith.title: Regolith shield
concept.regolith.capsule: Regolith is the loose dust and broken rock on top of the Mars ground. A thick pile of it over a shelter blocks much of the radiation.
concept.regolith.question: Piling ___ on a shelter helps block radiation.
concept.regolith.explain: A thick layer of Mars soil (regolith) is a shield we do not have to bring from Earth.
concept.flare.title: Solar flare and CME
concept.flare.capsule: A solar flare is a sudden bright flash on the Sun. A CME is a giant cloud of charged particles thrown out by the Sun. Both can send a particle storm toward Mars.
concept.flare.question: A giant cloud of particles thrown out by the Sun is called a ___.
concept.flare.explain: CME means coronal mass ejection: a huge cloud of charged particles from the Sun.
concept.rad.title: RAD
concept.rad.capsule: RAD is the radiation detector on the Curiosity rover. It has measured radiation on the Mars surface since 2012. The storm numbers in this game come from it.
concept.rad.question: Curiosity measures radiation with a tool called ___.
concept.rad.explain: RAD means Radiation Assessment Detector. Its real readings drive the storms in this game.
concept.gale.title: Gale Crater
concept.gale.capsule: Gale Crater is a huge old crater, about 154 km wide, with a tall mountain in the middle. Curiosity has explored it since 2012.
concept.gale.question: Curiosity landed inside ___ Crater.
concept.gale.explain: Curiosity landed in Gale Crater. (Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater.)
concept.delay.title: Message delay
concept.delay.capsule: Radio messages travel at the speed of light, but Mars is far away: a message takes about 3 to 22 minutes one way, depending on where the planets are.
concept.delay.question: A radio message from Earth reaches Mars in about ___.
concept.delay.explain: Light needs minutes to cross the gap, so Earth can never answer you at once.
concept.curiosity.title: Curiosity
concept.curiosity.capsule: Curiosity is a car-sized rover. It landed on Mars in August 2012 and is still exploring. It runs on nuclear power, not solar panels.
concept.curiosity.question: Curiosity is a ___ that explores Mars.
concept.curiosity.explain: A rover is a robot car that drives across another world.

hazard.isolation.name: Isolation

hazard.distance.name: Distance from Earth
hazard.distance.what: No quick deliveries: make your own air and food.
hazard.gravity.name: Gravity
hazard.gravity.what: Mars pulls only about 38% as hard as Earth.
hazard.hostile.name: Hostile, closed place
hazard.hostile.what: No air outside, cold and dust: the habitat keeps you safe.
hazard.title: 5 hazards of human spaceflight
hazard.source: Source: NASA Human Research Program, "5 hazards of human spaceflight"
storm.title: This storm was real
storm.w1: On 20 May 2024 a huge flare on the Sun sent a particle storm to Mars. Curiosity's RAD measured the biggest radiation jump since it landed in 2012.
storm.w2: In September 2017 the Sun threw out big flares. A particle storm reached Mars and Curiosity's RAD saw the radiation more than double.
storm.w3: In March 2023 particle storms hit near Earth, but Mars stayed quiet: the biggest rise RAD saw on Mars was small.

pick.w2: Big flares: radiation more than doubled at Mars.

sinfo.noActions: Nothing to do here: it is part of the story.
sinfo.notPlaced: Not built yet: get it from the store.
sinfo.habitat.what: Home: air to breathe, warmth at night and a bed for the crew.
sinfo.habitat.real: Real crews have practised a year-long Mars stay inside CHAPEA, a 3D-printed test habitat on Earth (2023-2024).
sinfo.habitat.hazard: Outside there is no air to breathe, and Mars nights can be colder than −70 °C.
sinfo.panels.what: Turn sunlight into power for the whole base.
sinfo.panels.real: The InSight lander's panels were slowly covered by Mars dust; its mission ended in 2022 when there was too little power.
sinfo.panels.hazard: No power plant on Mars: dust and storms dim the Sun, so keep the panels clean.
sinfo.moxie.what: Makes oxygen from the carbon dioxide in Mars air.
sinfo.moxie.real: MOXIE on the Perseverance rover really made oxygen on Mars: 122 grams between 2021 and 2023.
sinfo.moxie.hazard: Earth is far away: no air deliveries, so the base must make its own.
sinfo.greenhouse.what: Grows food under light and warmth.
sinfo.greenhouse.real: Astronauts on the International Space Station grow lettuce in the Veggie plant chamber and first ate it in 2015.
sinfo.greenhouse.hazard: Earth is far away: the crew must grow part of its own food.
sinfo.shelter.what: Thick walls of Mars soil (regolith) block particle storms.
sinfo.shelter.real: Mars has no global magnetic field and thin air, so particles from the Sun reach the ground. Curiosity's RAD measured a big storm on 20 May 2024.
sinfo.shelter.hazard: Radiation: wait inside the shelter while a particle storm passes.
sinfo.antenna.what: Sends messages to Earth and receives answers.
sinfo.antenna.real: A radio message needs about 3 to 22 minutes between Mars and Earth, depending on where the planets are.
sinfo.antenna.hazard: Isolation: answers come late, so the crew must plan ahead.
sinfo.beacon.what: Marks a safe landing spot for the rescue ship.
sinfo.beacon.real: Perseverance (2021) compared its camera pictures with a map while landing to pick a safe spot in Jezero Crater.
sinfo.beacon.hazard: Far from Earth: a ship can only land safely where the ground is known.
sinfo.curiosity.what: A real rover. Its radiation meter feeds the storm dose in this game.
sinfo.curiosity.real: Curiosity has explored Gale Crater since August 2012. Its RAD instrument measures radiation on the surface.
sinfo.curiosity.hazard: Radiation: the game's storm dose comes from RAD's real readings.
sinfo.science.what: Scan rocks to learn about Mars' past.
sinfo.science.real: Curiosity found old lake mud and clay in Gale Crater: water once stayed there for a long time.
sinfo.science.hazard: Cold, dusty and far from home: the walk takes longer.
sinfo.lander.what: The rocket that brought the crew. The parts for new stations come from it.
sinfo.lander.real: Plans for flying home from Mars need fuel made on Mars; MOXIE tested the first step by making oxygen.
sinfo.lander.hazard: Far from Earth: everything the base needs must come with the rocket or be made here.

gloss.sol: A sol is one day on Mars: about 24 hours and 39 minutes.
gloss.rad: RAD is the radiation meter on the Curiosity rover; it measures radiation on the ground of Mars.
gloss.regolith: Regolith is the loose dust and broken rock that covers the ground of Mars.
gloss.cme: A CME is a huge cloud of fast particles thrown out by the Sun; when it reaches Mars it brings a particle storm.
gloss.dose: Dose is how much radiation your body takes in; in this game the bar counts only the extra from storms.
gloss.moxie: MOXIE was a small machine on the Perseverance rover that made oxygen from the air of Mars.
gloss.curiosity: Curiosity is a car-sized rover that has explored Gale Crater on Mars since 2012.
gloss.gale: Gale Crater is a huge, very old crater on Mars; Curiosity landed there in 2012.

credits.intro: Every number in this game that is called real comes from the data sets below. Game rules (power, air, food, tasks) are simplified and labeled as game rules.
credits.sound: Sounds are made in code with the Web Audio API (no sound files). Fonts: system fonts.
credits.si: Made by team Seyir Defteri for the Space Apps Challenge 2026, with the help of an AI coding assistant. No AI-made images, video or audio.
